topic_coverage.quoted_user_text: Use a repo-root .env (gitignored) so SSH and Docker connection values exist for workflows that honor .cursor/remote.json and docs/engineering/release-targets.json. Ship .env.example with variable names only. Block AI from reading .env; allow starting ssh or other remote commands when the operator has already exported those vars into the shell.

Touch ignore rules (.gitignore, Cursor ignore for agents), runbook remote/release connectivity docs, optional Python or shell helpers that load .env for human/CI sessions, remote_config_summary contract, template copies of .env.example, and agent/rules text that forbids opening .env.

Keep US-0064 style: JSON files still reference env var names, not inline secrets. No credentials in git. Loading .env is operator-controlled; document that IDEs may not inject .env into agent context. Avoid duplicating release-targets schema inside .env keys beyond mapping already-named *Env fields.

Add acceptance for: .env gitignored; .env.example committed and free of secret literals; runbook procedure verified; regression that existing remote summary and release connectivity guidance still work when vars come from environment after sourcing .env outside the agent.

Operators copy .env.example to .env, fill values locally, source before remote work; remote.json and release-targets workflows document which *Env names map to .env keys; AI/rules explicitly do not read .env; template kit includes the same example and ignore entries.
